post.description:
Accept a claim: put the claimant on the member list and clear the pending tag.

The Initiative tag stays — they belong to the initiative, that was never in question; what
changes is that it is now confirmed. Adding the member without this leaves the pending tag
behind, and the "confirmed only" target group then keeps excluding the very person the head
just approved.

Idempotent: approving someone already on the list still clears the tag, which is how a
claim approved by hand before this route existed gets repaired.

InitiativeEventSchemaIn.description:
An initiative event as its head describes it.

Absent on purpose: the status (a create leaves a draft) and `is_initiative` (origin, not a
request). A client cannot express either, so there is no rule to enforce afterwards.

The audience is chosen, but only from `Audience` — one of this initiative's three
preconfigured groups, resolved by the server. A `TargetGroup` uuid is still not accepted:
"which of your members" must never widen into "any group in the CRM".

`event_hidden` *is* here. Putting an event on the public page is allowed — it costs the
head the auto-publish and sends the event to approval instead, which is the rule the
document describes rather than a prohibition.

event_hidden.description: True keeps the event off the public landing page. Setting it False is allowed but costs the auto-publish: the event then needs team approval via PUT /api/v1/events/review/{uuid}. Frozen once the event is Active.
event_hidden.title: Event Hidden

target_group_variant.description: Which slice of the initiative to reach: 'all' every member, 'confirmed' every member except unconfirmed claims, 'heads' only the initiative's heads. Resolved server-side to that initiative's preconfigured group; a TargetGroup uuid is not accepted. Omit for 'all'. Frozen once the event is Active.

qr_sent_on.description: When attendees receive their QR ticket. Null disables ticketing. The door scanner links are emailed to scanner_emails at qr_scanner_send_at.

scanner_emails.description: Who receives the door-scanner link, one or more. Every address must be on this initiative's member list. Required — and only required — when qr_scanner_send_at is set: scheduling a scanner send with nobody to send it to is a silent no-op. There is no default: guessing would hand the door to whoever happened to be marked head first. An Organizer id is never accepted here — the Organizer table is the Frankie team's.
scanner_emails.title: Scanner Emails

ProactiveRequestSchemaIn.description:
`initiative` and `status` are absent on purpose: the account decides the first and the
server the second. A payload naming either is ignored rather than honoured.

FrankieUserMatchSchema.description:
Whether this member is a Frankie user, and on what evidence.

Always present: `match_type` is "unknown" rather than the object being null, so the
frontend has one shape to render instead of two.
FrankieUserMatchSchema.title: FrankieUserMatchSchema

InitiativeMemberCreateSchemaIn.description: Adding one member. `initiative` is absent on purpose — it comes from the account.

InitiativeMemberUpdateSchemaIn.description:
Partial update: only the fields present in the body are written.

`initiative` is absent on purpose — moving a row between initiatives would cross the
boundary the whole guard exists to enforce.
InitiativeMemberUpdateSchemaIn.title: InitiativeMemberUpdateSchemaIn

PendingMemberSchemaOut.description: Someone who says they belong to an initiative but is not on its member list.
PendingMemberSchemaOut.title: PendingMemberSchemaOut

PendingResolveSchemaIn.description:
Resolving a claim identifies the *claimant*, not a member to create.

Deliberately not the member schema: approve is a different action from create. The name,
email and matrikelnumber come from the profile that made the claim, so a head cannot
approve one person into the list under another person's details. Only the role is theirs
to choose.
